title_original: MIA Photo Fair 2027, The 16th Edition With An International Scope

blocks.text: Unveiled during Paris Photo, the sixteenth edition of MIA Photo Fair BNP Paribas, Italy’s leading art fair dedicated to photography, will bring together exhibitions, awards and talks in Milan from 18 to 21 March 2027.

One international photography event announces another. Reflecting the growing ties between Paris Photo and MIA Photo Fair BNP Paribas, the main highlights of the Italian fair’s sixteenth edition were unveiled in France on 12 November. The occasion also provided an opportunity to strengthen the international dimension of the Milan event. “ Photography has the power to cross borders, tell stories of identity and forge new connections, ” emphasised Ludovico Serra, Chargé d’Affaires at the Italian Embassy. “ Presenting MIA Photo Fair in Paris, at the heart of one of the most important international photography events, means putting this vision into practice and strengthening the dialogue between Italy and France through culture. ”

From 18 to 21 March 2027, MIA Photo Fair will place belonging, relationships and attachment at the heart of its sixteenth edition. Belonging. Storie di appartenenza will be its main theme, explored through exhibitions, special projects, awards and new partnerships. Two Pairs of Eyes. Photographs by Donata and Wim Wenders will be among the highlights, featuring a selection of images by the two photographers. Brought together for the first time, their works will offer “ a silent but deeply moving exchange: sometimes surprisingly close, sometimes marked by different perceptions, but always united by a shared sensitivity, attentive to the extraordinary that reveals itself in the most ordinary moments of everyday life, ” according to the organisers.

Italian photographer Nino Migliori will also be honoured on the occasion of his centenary. The creator of the image featured in the visual identity of this new edition, he will be the subject of a retrospective tracing one of the most distinctive careers on the international art scene, from his realist photographs of the 1950s to his experiments with photographic language.

To extend this photographic exploration, the event will also highlight the photographers and organisations that contribute to the vitality of the medium through a series of prizes and awards. The third edition of the Image Media Excellence Award 2027 , which supports media outlets pioneering innovative uses of imagery and visual design in journalism, will be presented to the biannual magazine Lampoon . Recognised for its critical and independent perspective on the languages of fashion, design and contemporary culture, the magazine will present an exhibition devoted to censorship, explored through photography and contemporary art.

Around ten other awards, established over successive editions, will once again support artists and galleries. Among them, the Premio Collezione Ettore Molinario is evolving into an acquisition prize: the winning work will enter La Collezione Ettore Molinario, which will itself be highlighted through a selection of photographs exploring the theme of Belonging .

This sixteenth edition continues the curatorial research undertaken in recent years, affirming photography as a meeting point between artistic research, the art market and visual culture. Italian and international galleries will be presented alongside video and digital installations, as well as a section dedicated to the evolution of documentary language. The Circuito OFF programme will also continue to extend the event’s presence throughout the city.

Last year, the fair brought together more than 500 artists, 111 exhibitors and 76 galleries, attracting some 10,000 visitors. The ambition of Francesca Malgara, director of MIA Photo Fair BNP Paribas, remains unchanged: “ to give Milan an increasingly prominent place on the international photography scene. The city has an exceptional visual culture, shaped by art, design, fashion and publishing, and has much to offer those discovering it. ”
